title: Elections board chair announces departure, new chair takes the reins
summary: Maryland State Board of Elections Chair Michael G. Summers announced Thursday that he plans to leave the five-member board, leaving it evenly divided between two Democrats and two Republicans and likely setting off a scramble to replace him.
content:
by Bryan P. Sears, Maryland Matters July 23, 2026

by Bryan P. Sears, Maryland Matters July 23, 2026

Maryland State Board of Elections Chair Michael G. Summers announced Thursday that he will leave the board on July 31, leaving the five-member board evenly split for now between Democratic and Republican members.

Summers’ announcement came the same day the board was meeting to certify the results of last month’s primary elections and almost four months before the 2026 general election. It also came nearly two years before the end of Summers’ term, which was set for 2028

In brief comments, Summers said there was a “conflict of commitent” between his board commitments and his personal life, and he was stepping down to focus “on my personal development, and I’ve gottne quite a bit more responsibility than I can handle.”

After announcing he was leaving, Summers moved to hand the chairmanship over to board member Victoria Jackson-Stanley, a fellow Democrat and the former mayor of Cambridge. The board unanimously accepted the motion and Jackson-Stanley ran the rest of meeting as chair.

Summers’ resignation is likely to touch off an effort to fill the spot before November, as any decision made by the board requires four votes from the board. The board majority is determined by the party of the governor, so any replacement for Summers would be a Democrat.

Summers, 53, served as a member of the House of Delegates from 2011-2015, representing Prince George’s County. During his time in the House he was assigned to the House Ways and Means Committee, serving on the panel’s subcommittee on elections. He was also the deputy majority whip for the final two years of his term.

According to his LinkedIn page, he currently works as director of grants management for the Corps Network, formerly the National Association of Service and Conservation Corps.
